CHIEF COMPLAINT
Right elbow pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient is a male who injured his right elbow approximately one week ago while playing lacrosse with his children. He was throwing a ball when the pain started. He reports that his 13-year-old son may have struck him several times with a lacrosse stick. Pain is localized to the tip/point of the elbow and is sharp in character, worsening with any movement. Pain radiates down the forearm. Patient took Advil for a couple of days and reports it provided some relief. Patient also presents with hypertension; blood pressure today is 150/90, which is elevated. He attributes this possibly to white coat syndrome.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Denies chest pain. Denies abdominal pain. Lungs clear bilaterally. Heart exam reveals grade 2 out of 6 systolic ejection murmur, which is known.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Hypertension. Diabetes mellitus. Systolic ejection murmur.

MEDICATIONS
Lisinopril 20 mg daily for hypertension. Metformin 500 mg daily for diabetes.

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient has two children, ages 13 and 10. He plays lacrosse with his children. He and his family follow a Mediterranean diet with low salt intake and avoid adding salt to food. He reports good compliance with dietary modifications. He does not take insulin and does not check blood sugar daily; when checked, blood sugars run between 80-100.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Blood pressure: 150/90. Lungs: clear bilaterally. Heart: grade 2 out of 6 systolic ejection murmur. Right elbow: pain to palpation over the olecranon area of the posterior elbow, mild pain with flexion and extension, normal range of motion, mild swelling and bruising present.

RESULTS
X-ray of right elbow: normal, no fracture, no bony abnormality.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Right elbow contusion from lacrosse stick trauma. Prescribed ibuprofen 800 mg twice daily for pain and swelling. Ice elbow three times daily for 20 minutes per session. Avoid playing lacrosse for the next couple of weeks to allow healing. Continue lisinopril 20 mg daily for hypertension management. Continue metformin 500 mg daily for diabetes management. Order A1C test to assess glycemic control and determine if medication adjustment is needed in the future.
